newsitem.title: UK: Copper falls again on LME, at 7-1/2 month low.
newsitem.headline: Copper falls again on LME, at 7-1/2 month low.

text.p: Copper prices fell further during Monday LME evening inter-office trading, as a sickly market ignored oversold technicals and dropped to the lowest levels since the start of the year.

Traders said the market extended the current fall from levels near $2,300 only last Thursday on renewed speculative liquidation. The fresh decline from kerb closing levels of $2,162 entailed sell-stops below $2,150.
The current weak trend reflects continued increases in LME warehouse stocks, slow summer physicals, and the re-emergence of a cash/threes contango on the LME.
There is also some nervousness over the current falls in global equity markets, some said.
At 1800 gmt three months copper was indicated at $2,135/2,140 a tonne, against the $2,162 kerb close and last Friday's $2,213 finish.
Aluminium eased back as well from kerb closing levels, but was cautious over the cash/threes backwardation, which virtually doubled on Monday. It was indicated at $1,666/1,670.
